build.redEvidence:
Reproduced before any product edit (worktree at 84afe34, d1c7da0 is an ancestor).

(a) WIRE. frontend/libs/api-client/src/client.test.ts builds the real createApiClient with a stubbed fetch and calls delivery.trips.settle with day-end.tsx's input. It FAILED:
"AssertionError: trip 01924f9a-0000-7000-8000-0000000000d1, new settlement id 01a09bb9-6e45-7353-a328-483191d4c112"
- Expected url "/delivery/trips/01924f9a-0000-7000-8000-0000000000d1/settle"; received "/delivery/trips/01a09bb9-6e45-7353-a328-483191d4c112/settle", which is the new settlement id.
- The body had no "id" and carried "tripId": "01924f9a-...d1".

(b) SERVER PROBE. A temporary test named "DOS-112 today's settle wire request is refused" sent the request the link builds today, then was deleted before commit. Output saved in the scratchpad file dos112-probe.txt:
"POST /delivery/trips/01a09bbb-6583-739f-bc8a-a037dfa4c986/settle → 400 {"message":"the id in the URL (\"01a09bbb-6583-739f-bc8a-a037dfa4c986\") does not match the tripId in the body (\"01a09bbb-6523-76b5-b14b-1248a4052997\")","error":"Bad Request","statusCode":400}"
- The test also asserted that exact message and that the trip stayed `closing`.

(c) COMMITTED SERVER TEST on today's code. The request is POST /delivery/trips/<tripId>/settle with body {id: <settlementId>, idempotencyKey, handedOverCashPaise, acceptVariance, note} and no tripId, exactly what the link sends after the fix. It FAILED:
"{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","status":400,"message":"Input validation failed","data":{"issues":[{"path":["tripId"],"message":"Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"}]}}: expected 400 to be 200"
- Cause: the route still named its segment {id}, so the trip id in the path was read as `id`, overwritten by the body's id, and tripId never arrived.
- An earlier run failed in the test setup instead: "a trip with no stops only makes sense with van sales enabled". I fixed the setup and re-ran to get the failure above.

steps.observed: day-end.tsx never sends `counted`, and the server counts every lot missing from `counted` as zero. So if the closing trip's van still holds stock, the manager will get 409 settlement_needs_owner and an approvals row, not a success. For a clean success, pick a closing trip whose vehicle location has no on-hand stock. Then run: cd QA/tools && DATABASE_URL=postgres://dos:dos@127.0.0.1:5439/dos_qa node e2e/dos-112-settle-probe.mjs (TRIP_ID=<id> to pin one).
